quest.title: The Exile: Sprouting
quest.description: The Sumeru Roses planted by Sabbah never grow. Try to help her.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Ziyad
dialogues.text: ♪Rose, oh rose, grant me my wish.

dialogues.speaker: Ziyad
dialogues.text: ♪Blooming from a stone, the Golden Rose sang to me.

dialogues.speaker: Ziyad
dialogues.text: ♪She sang...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's a local Sumeru folk song called the "Singing Rose," right? It's such a cute song.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Too bad the boy ran off halfway through. Paimon would have loved to hear the whole thing and say hi to him.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: You must be new here. First time in Aaru Village?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: No wonder you've never heard of that folk song.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Well then, are you scholars looking to study abroad in Sumeru? I know that there are many foreign scholars in the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We do know a lot of scholars, but we aren't quite like them ourselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Technically, we're adventurers, the glorious world-trotting duo — Paimon and {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: World-trotting? Hahaha!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's so funny? We're super famous adventurers, believe it or not.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: No, I wasn't mocking you, friends from faraway. Just the opposite. It's a delight to hear uplifting stories like people traveling the world.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: When you're as detached from the world as I am, such enthusiastic remarks can really catch you off guard.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I'm sorry if I offended you. My name is Sabbah. I offer you my apologies as well as my welcome to the village.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Ah yes. Were you talking about the rose folk song that Ziyad was singing?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: We can talk more about it if you're interested. I hope it will liven up your journey.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you going to sing for us, Sabbah? Paimon's dying to hear the rest of it!

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Sorry, I'm not good at singing... But we can discuss what the song is about.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure! So, that kid sang about the rose granting wishes...

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Yes. In a tiny village like ours, we don't have a big athenaeum like they do at the Akademiya. All our songs are passed down orally.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: It's my belief that the wish-granting flower in the song represents the collective imagination of our ancestors.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: In a harsh environment like the desert, water is an extremely vital resource, so they prized water-storing plants.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: So, the more adverse the terrain, the more stories there are about plants. It's a reflection of our ancestors' yearning for a better life.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: At the same time, plants are also a part of the symbiotic relationship between our ancestors and the flora and fauna of the desert.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: However... Aaru is built on sand and the soil here is actually not suitable for the cultivation of Sumeru Roses.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: The Sumeru Roses I planted could never grow, so if you ask me, the Golden Rose in the song must have been a product of people's imagination...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, hold on, Paimon can't keep up anymore...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this what you usually talk with people about, Miss Sabbah?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Ah! I'm sorry, I thought since you were new here, you'd prefer such topics over farming or the weather.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon got lost somewhere between "symbiotic relationship" and "the collective imagination," but don't worry, Paimon understood that last sentence!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You said that the land here isn't suitable for Sumeru Roses, right? We've also only seen them in places with moist soil.

choices.text: Well, this place is mostly sand, after all.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Speaking of roses, I was thinking that since you two are adventurers, perhaps I can hire you to...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now we're talking! We're battle-hardened adventurers. We can do any job, no problem!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, what can we help you with?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I know it's ridiculous to want roses that don't belong here to bloom, but regardless, I still really want to see them.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I'm embarrassed to even say it, but that is my wish.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Based on what I know about roses, they will grow if fertilized with highly concentrated Dendro, even if you grow them in sand.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: But it's near-impossible to get such fertilizer out here, so I'm wondering if you may be able to get your hands on some...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Dendro?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Yes, Dendro promotes plant growth and works especially well on poor crops.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: But I'm just a normal person without a Dendro Vision, and I lack the resources to obtain effective fertilizer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. If it's just <color=#00E1FFFF>Dendro</color> you want, this is pretty easy! We got this!

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Huh? Did I guess wrong? Let me think again...

talks.objective: Use the power of Dendro to "fertilize" the seeds

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Can you wield Dendro? Are you someone with a Vision?

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I haven't met anyone like that in a long time. What a nostalgic feeling...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It should be fine now, right, Miss Sabbah?

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: That's right, they should sprout soon if powered by Dendro. Let's just wait for a while...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Gradually, sprouts begin peeking out of the soil.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: They stop growing after sprouting a few leaves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #They're sprouting! Paimon knew you could do just about anything, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: The results were immediate, as I thought... Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Too bad there are no flowers yet.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Oh, that's normal. You can't rush such things.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Plants have to go through stages of growth. That you were able to make them sprout is already quite amazing.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Give the roses some more time to take in the nourishment. It will be better for them as well.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: I'm very grateful to you as it is. I wouldn't wish to bother you further.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Just drop by and see them in your spare time. That would be enough.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: If it weren't for you, I don't think I'd have ever seen these roses sprout.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: If only I knew this would happen... instead of seeds, I should have brought a few more books.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Are you surprised? Well, I guess that means that I've adapted pretty well.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: When I first got here, I was unable to get used to anything, whether it be the food, the housing, or anything else.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: But I got used to everything over time.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: That doesn't mean that I've fully accepted my predicament, though.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I suppose it is impossible to make roses from Sumeru City bloom here after all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you a researcher?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I could have been called that once, but not anymore.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I said something beyond my station, and learned something I shouldn't have.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I broke the Akademiya's taboos, so I was removed from amongst their ranks.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What did you say?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Curiosity is the impetus for seeking wisdom, but it's also the cause of sin.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I only understood that after I was exiled to this place.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: For safety reasons, I don't think I should go into details.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: All right then.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Ahem, but...

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I thought adventurers would just come and go, never coming back to chit-chat after finishing their jobs.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I didn't expect to have another long conversation with you.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: To be honest, I don't have a lot of friends to talk to here.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: Do you think... at some point... you would be able to come by and fertilize my plants again?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: ...Okay then, I'll wait for you.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: You probably don't know much about them... but they are very versatile, and have many uses.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: They can be eaten, turned into medicine, given as gifts, or fetch a good price on the market.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: And that's just some of the more common applications.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: The flower, leaves, and stalk of a Sumeru Rose also did not always look like this. They all had different appearances once upon a time.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I believe geographical changes led to changes in the roses' traits.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: A study of its traits could help us derive past geographical and historical information.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I won't be able to explain the mechanism over just a casual conversation, and sharing such information with adventurers is probably against the rules as well.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: If you're interested in botanical evolution, you should visit the Akademiya. They'll have more on the subject.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, you're doing this for your research?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I'm not a researcher anymore. I no longer have the right or means to pursue any research.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: If you must know why... *sigh*, you are a very curious soul, you know that?

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: I grew a lot of Sumeru Roses back in my former residence. The flowers were spectacular, and I got to see them every day.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: If it was possible, I wish I could see them again, just like before.

response.speaker: Sabbah
response.text: ...That's all there is to it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I can understand that.

dialogues.speaker: Sabbah
dialogues.text: Do you really have a way to grow roses through the power of <color=#00E1FFFF>Dendro</color>?
